outcome: Need for cardiac intervention before hospital discharge
cohort: The study included 157 fetuses with prenatally diagnosed congenital heart disease (CHD) at a single center.
finding: Maternal-infant bonding was found to be safe for select infants with prenatally diagnosed CHD and was associated with shorter hospital and ICU lengths of stay, and higher survival rates.
mod_finding: Infants who were unsuccessful at bonding were more likely to have been delivered via Caesarean section (74% versus 49%, p=0.011).
birth_weight: Successful bonders averaged 3.26 kg, while those unsuccessful at bonding averaged 2.6 kg.
gest_age: Successful bonders averaged 39 weeks gestation, while those unsuccessful averaged 38 weeks.
